notes:
Summary:
- Mid-market SaaS (product onboarding copilots). Evaluating Hosted API first (fast time-to-value) then Dedicated if cost/predictability warrants.
- Primary ask: in-app guided flows (step-by-step onboarding assistant) with strict per-session token caps and predictable streaming latency.

Timeline / recent activity:
- 2026-01-15: Intro call (Ava) — product summary, high-level infra needs.
- 2026-02-05: Demo (live) of Redwood hosted streaming + function calling (FF transcript ff_2026-02-20_BridgeDemo). AE notes: "streaming looked smooth but UI showed a 2nd-token delay occasionally".
- 2026-02-18: Security questionnaire returned (legal note re: EU data subsets & KMS). Jira SEC-1107 opened.
- 2026-03-01: POC kickoff — 2-week perf test using hosted endpoints. Tests: 500 concurrent sessions simulating guided flows, heavy tool-calling to Product Catalog API.
- 2026-03-08: Interim POC check-in with Marcus (SE) — initial metrics collected, p50 token latency ~180ms, p95 ~760ms on peak; streaming start time inconsistent under burst.

Requirements / desired outcomes:
- Workload: interactive chat/agent used inside product onboarding — many short turns, lots of tool calls (lookup, suggestions, structured outputs).
- Latency SLO: p50 end-to-end token/stream start <= 250ms; p95 < 700ms desirable. Consistent tail latency more important than absolute best-case.
- Throughput: support steady 60-120 qps for onboarding sessions during workday peaks; burst to 250 qps tolerated.
- Cost sensitivity: per-MAU cost cap target so token cost caps per-session = 1500-2000 tokens; want Redwood Optimize recommendations to hit cost target (target ARR math: keep per-user inference cost < $0.30/mo at scale).
- Feature asks: robust streaming, reliable function/tool calling (deterministic tool timeouts), prefix/KV cache for repeat flows, model fallbacks for graceful degradation.
- Compliance: SSO (SAML/Okta), audit logs, optional customer-managed KMS, EU data residency for certain customers.

POC scope / metrics being captured:
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 for streaming start and token generation, cold vs warm cache.
- Token usage: tokens/session distribution, abandoned session waste.
- Tool calling reliability: success rate, end-to-end time (including product catalog call).
- Cost projection: estimated monthly token spend vs ARR targets.

Quotes / call snippets:
- "If we can't guarantee a snappy, predictable first-word experience the product feels laggy — that's our main risk." — Head of Product
- "We need a plan to cap token spend per session; users are on guided flows of 6-10 turns on average." — Growth lead

Sales / commercial notes:
- Primary path: start on Hosted API (self-serve + AE support) -> if POC shows sustained usage and pricing fits, move to Dedicated reserved pool (monthly commit).
- Pricing convo scheduled w/ Finance on 2026-03-15. Expect request for committed throughput discount and an SLO/Billing credit clause.
- Potential upsell: Redwood Console retention & Optimize add-on for automated batching/quantization recommendations.

Open items / blockers:
- Action: SE to run targeted p95 tail reduction experiments (kernel config + batching) and share config by 2026-03-12.
- Legal: clarify EU residency approach and KMS integration latency impact (SEC-1107).
- Pricing: need modeled ARR vs unit-cost scenarios for two commit levels (50k and 150k ARR).

Next steps:
- 2026-03-12: Marcus to deliver tuned POC config + recommended model/quantization pairings.
- 2026-03-15: Pricing review with Finance + AE (Ava).
- 2026-03-22: Decision gate — proceed to Dedicated eval or continue on Hosted with optimization.
public_notes: Evaluating Hosted -> Dedicated; focus on streaming latency SLOs and token cost caps for in-app onboarding copilots. POC running, SE experiments scheduled, pricing review mid-March.
